answer: At dawn, a verifier accepts an agent only when its signing key is bound to a fresh SGX/SEV attestation: the MRENCLAVE (or SEV launch measurement) must match approved code, and a hardware-rooted credential identifies the platform. Copying a VM image reproduces code, not that credential; under a one-identity-per-platform policy, adding accepted identities requires additional physical silicon, not virtual duplication. A vertex registry detects reused credentials, so a sparrow agent cannot multiply by copying files.
